assumptions: The initial product remains non-custodial and limited to reconciliation, accounting support, and dispute evidence rather than funds movement, tax advice, or binding dispute decisions.
A target customer already has lawful authority to share the relevant private CDR, tariff, agreement, and invoice data; AFIR public-data access alone is insufficient.
The founder can use specialized protocol, security, VAT, and legal contractors within the stated capital constraint while retaining final product ownership.
The initial beachhead is limited to direct or multi-platform charging relationships with exceptions not already resolved by an incumbent hub.
No customer, channel, pricing, retention, or operational-effort validation exists beyond the supplied research.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Two or more paired-counterparty pilots using historical and live authorized data should document the incumbent-uncovered exception rate and value, baseline labor, recovered or prevented loss, resolution-speed improvement, evidence acceptance, onboarding and support hours, security requirements, and a signed recurring willingness-to-pay commitment; at least one integrator should also demonstrate a repeatable channel to similar accounts.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Residual full, partial, off-platform, and unpaid reconciliation cases are directly evidenced, so cross-platform evidence lineage is a plausible gap. However, protocol normalization and the broad clearing workflow are established rather than novel, and the existence of a valuable independent-supplier gap remains an inference.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Incorrect settlement, disputed sessions, and manual reconciliation can cause cash leakage and labor cost, and incumbent clearing products confirm that the job matters. The supplied evidence does not establish uncovered exception frequency, monetary loss, budget ownership, or willingness to pay a neutral entrant, while low-priced incumbent coverage may already satisfy much of the need.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Recurring charging records and a non-custodial software model could support repeat usage without funding settlement balances. Yet pricing, gross margin, acquisition cost, retention, payback, support effort, and obtainable customer count are all unknown; bespoke mappings, security, VAT-boundary work, and manual dispute review could make this a services-heavy business, and incumbent transaction pricing constrains monetization.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Small and mid-sized Polish or CEE operators using direct or multiple-platform relationships form a reasonably specific initial segment. No evidence quantifies how many such relationships exist, how many lack adequate incumbent coverage, or whether their recoverable value supports a meaningful standalone market; fragmentation may also make each account unusually bespoke.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Vendor-neutral reconciliation across multiple hubs could occupy a narrow position if counterparties accept its evidence. Gireve already markets nearly the complete workflow, Hubject provides EU-wide financial services and manual reconciliation, and both protocol standards encode much of the proposed record, giving incumbents strong customer access and an easy path to extend exception tooling.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Successful integrations and accepted evidence could extend into additional operators, fleets, countries, dispute analytics, and back-office workflows. Expansion is not frictionless: each platform, bilateral contract, and jurisdiction can add new permissions, mappings, tax configuration, security requirements, and incumbent competition.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: A permissioned edge-case library, bilateral mappings, resolution history, and embedded accounting integrations could improve automation and create switching friction over time. These inputs are unlikely to be exclusive, mature standards reduce the proprietary surface, and established hubs possess larger networks, data flows, and customer relationships from which to build similar capabilities.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Independent cross-platform lineage could be useful where no single hub sees the full transaction chain. There is no evidence of a material improvement in recovery, resolution speed, accuracy, price, or audit acceptance, while incumbents already provide CDR checks, agreement-based calculation, invoicing, clearing, and dispute support.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Growing standardized EV-roaming data flows and formalized infrastructure-data obligations create more recurring records and make integrations more tractable. The same protocol maturity commoditizes normalization, public-data rules do not unlock private settlement records, and incumbent clearing products are already mature, so timing helps the category more than this entrant specifically.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: A read-only pilot through a charger back-office integrator is a plausible focused route and does not require a public-facing founder brand. No integrator or operator has committed, private access is contractual, counterparties may need to participate together, and security and trust reviews can create long sales cycles that conflict with a part-time founder.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: Data normalization, anomaly detection, and evidence lineage fit the founder, and a tightly bounded non-custodial pilot may be feasible with the available capital. Execution still depends on private-data rights, protocol and back-office mappings, security and GDPR controls, cross-border invoice boundaries, counterparty acceptance, and domain expertise; bespoke support could exceed the founder's available time.

highest_value_structural_change: Recast the offer as a white-label exception-evidence module distributed through one back-office integrator that already has authorized access across direct and multiple-hub feeds, and build the generalized product only after the integrator's customers show measured incremental recoveries or labor savings that incumbent platforms do not deliver.
main_structural_strength: A precise, non-custodial wedge around evidence lineage across direct and multiple roaming platforms, aligned with the founder's data-normalization skills and testable through a read-only pilot.
primary_score_limiter: There is no evidence that a sufficiently large set of operators simultaneously has costly gaps left by incumbents, can authorize the necessary private bilateral feeds, and will pay an independent entrant to resolve them.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Gireve directly markets CDR quality checks, agreement-based price calculation, B2B invoicing, payment tracking, and dispute management, while Hubject already provides broad European OCPI/OICP clearing and documents exception reconciliation; this places nearly the entire proposed job inside established platforms.
